newsitem.title: CANADA: PanCanadian to buy CS Resources for C$465 million.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian to buy CS Resources for C$465 million.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd. played white knight on Wednesday to CS Resources Ltd., agreeing to acquire it in a $521 million ($376 million) deal that topped a rival bid from Gulf Canada Resources Ltd..

PanCanadian will pay C$16 ($11.52) a share or C$465 million ($335 million) in cash and assume C$56 million ($40 million) of CS debt. The friendly transaction was approved by the boards of PanCanadian and CS.
After PanCanadian announced its offer, Gulf Canada said it would not increase its C$413 million ($301 million) hostile bid launched earlier this month for CS.
"We just simply are not going to raise our bid. The value may be there for PanCanadian, but it's not there for Gulf," Gulf Canada Chief Executive J.P. Bryan told Reuters.
Gulf Canada's bid of C$14.25 ($10.27) a share in cash and stock was set to expire on July 8. Calgary, Alberta-based Gulf Canada acquired Britain's Clyde Petroleum earlier this year in a bitter fight.
Shares of Calgary-based CS were up C90 cents to C$15.85 on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Wednesday, topping actives on more than 5.3 million shares.
PanCanadian was down C10 cents to C$30.10 in Toronto, while Gulf Canada rose C10 cents to C$11.80.
"This acquisition will combine the strengths of two of Canada's leading heavy oil producers," PanCanadian Chief Executive David Tuer said.
"We believe that PanCanadian's offer price will be highly attractive to our shareholders and is certainly a fair price," CS Chief Executive Dennis Sharp said in a joint statement.
In a telephone conference call with reporters, Tuer said Sharp agreed to continue his "association" with CS after the takeover.

Tuer said that if its bid succeeded, Calgary-based PanCanadian planned to combine its drilling expertise with CS's "high-potential" heavy oil and oilsands properties to form a "distinct heavy oil arm" at PanCanadian.
PanCanadian's offer represented a 41.6 percent premium over the closing price of CS shares on June 5, the day before Gulf Canada announced its bid, the companies said.
The PanCanadian offer was also a 17 percent premium over the value of Gulf Canada's cash and share offer based on Gulf's closing price on June 17, they said.
The offer is conditional on 66-2/3 percent of CS's shares being tendered.

PanCanadian, which does not own any CS Resources shares, said it would pay for the acquisition from existing cash balances. PanCanadian is 87 percent-owned by Montreal-based conglomerate Canadian Pacific Ltd., which on Monday sold its stake in waste disposal company Laidlaw Inc. to underwriters for C$1.05 billion ($756 million).
CS has reported proved and one-half probable crude oil reserves of 132 million barrels and 44 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
Based on first-quarter reports, the combined daily production of the new PanCanadian would be about 155,000 barrels of oil and liquids and 738 million cubic feet of natural gas, the company said.
